rounds.text: CHL Ltd is trading at a compelling valuation of 9.01x P/E [E1] and 0.75x book value [E2], with its P/B ratio sitting at a steep discount to the sector benchmark of 0.95x [E7]. The company is virtually debt-free with zero borrowings [E38, E39], and its fundamental quality is underscored by a robust 5-year compounded profit growth of 35% that easily outpaces its 5-year share price growth of 21% [E19, E23]. Recent quarterly metrics highlight a strong operational rebound, featuring expanding margins [E68] where operating margin reached 26% in Mar 2026 compared to 21% in the year-ago quarter [E31], alongside stellar cash conversion of 1.19x backing profits entirely with ₹ 19 Cr in operating cash flow [E34, E35]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow analysis implies an intrinsic value of ₹ 119 per share against the market price of ₹ 26.6, offering a substantial 77.6% margin of safety [E44, E45], while a reverse DCF indicates the current price pessimistically assumes a -2.8% earnings growth against the 18.0% base case [E46]. Conceded: [E6] P/E of 353.75x against a sector benchmark of 32.02x, [E17] compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months of -12%, [E21] compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months of -37%, and [E63] earnings that include other income of ₹ 14.7 Cr.

The fundamental performance of CHL Ltd exhibits severe structural deterioration despite any headline optical value, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month sales contraction of 12% [E17] and a staggering 37% collapse in trailing twelve-month profit growth [E21]. Profitability metrics are exceptionally weak, evidenced by a miserable ROE of 0.1% against a sector benchmark of 8.4% [E9], a pathetic ROA of -0.01% [E8], and a multi-year operating margin compression from 31% down to 11% [E30]. Furthermore, reported earnings quality is heavily compromised by the inclusion of Rs. 14.7 Cr in other income [E63], masking underlying core operational weakness while the company stubbornly refuses to pay any dividends to shareholders [E4, E61]. Technical momentum confirms this fundamental rot, as the stock languishes at the absolute bottom of its 52-week range (0% of range) [E47], trades well below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E49], and suffers from a dreadful relative-strength rating of just 5 against the Nifty 500 [E50]. Conceded: the company boasts a pristine debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x alongside solid operating cash flow backed by profits [E34, E38], yet this balance sheet safety has completely failed to generate any meaningful shareholder returns or price appreciation.
